data.title: Paraguay's ex-President Peña faces prosecutors after impeachment, house arrest
data.description:
Paraguay’s former President Santiago Peña arrived at the Attorney General’s Office on Saturday to appear before prosecutors, a day after he was impeached and placed under house arrest amid a political and financial crisis triggered by the collapse of digital lender ueno.

Prosecutors said on Friday that charges against Peña were still being determined but could include influence peddling.

His removal brought Vice President Pedro Alliana to power, with the longtime ruling Colorado Party politician sworn in on Friday to complete Peña’s term through August 2028.

Lawmakers who backed Peña’s impeachment accused him of conflicts of interest, manipulating regulatory oversight and participating in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.

Peña, who was a shareholder in ueno’s holding company until March 2025, has denied wrongdoing and said the bank’s problems were a regulatory matter.

The collapse has left millions of customers struggling to access their accounts and prompted protests in Asuncion. The scandal has also swept up senior officials and former ueno executives, while regulators have sought to reassure depositors and contain risks to the wider financial system.

data.title: E20 petrol supplied by PSU oil firms meets prescribed quality standards: Oil Min
data.description:
The government on Saturday defended the 20 per cent ethanol-blended petrol programme, saying tests of 893 samples collected across 27 states and Union Territories, including 56 in Karnataka, found them compliant with prescribed quality standards, as state-run oil companies challenged the Karnataka government's claims of excessive ethanol content in fuel sold at some retail outlets.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, in a statement, said Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) had found ethanol content in all 893 samples within the prescribed 19-21 per cent range under the Bureau of Indian Standards' IS 17021 specification.

The 56 samples tested in Karnataka, covering different locations and all three oil marketing companies (OMCs), recorded ethanol content of 19-20 per cent, averaging 19.30 per cent, the ministry said.

The findings directly contradict a recent press release by Karnataka's Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology, which claimed that petrol samples collected from certain retail outlets in the state contained 26-31 per cent ethanol.

The three OMCs have questioned the sampling and testing procedures adopted in Karnataka's October 2026 exercise, arguing that the reported results cannot be independently validated without compliance with prescribed statutory procedures and disclosure of the technical details of the tests.

The dispute comes at a time when India's nationwide E20 programme, aimed at reducing dependence on imported crude oil and lowering emissions, has come under scrutiny over concerns about vehicle mileage, engine compatibility and the potential cost to consumers.

Under the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, read with the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024, six one-litre samples must be drawn during an inspection. Two are handed to the dealer, two retained by the oil company or department, and two sent to an authorised laboratory.

The OMCs said samples collected during a September exercise were routed through the State Level Coordinator to designated company laboratories, but the subsequent October exercise was reportedly conducted without their representatives.

They said they had not received the corresponding retention samples, complete outlet-wise details or laboratory reports despite seeking them through the State Level Coordinator.

The companies also questioned certificates issued by a third-party laboratory, saying these did not specify the standard test method, dilution procedure or reference material used to determine ethanol content through Gas Chromatography.

Under IS 17021:2018, amended in August 2025, ethanol content must be determined through specified methods, including Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, water extraction or Gas Chromatography under prescribed ASTM standards.

When Gas Chromatography is used, the standard requires samples to be diluted in a 1:1 ratio with oxygenate-free petrol and results corrected against an E10 certified reference material, the OMCs said.

The companies also flagged density readings of 0.742-0.749 grams per cubic centimetre in samples reportedly containing 26-31% ethanol, compared with 0.752-0.760 grams per cubic centimetre in their own E20 samples. Since ethanol is denser than petrol, a higher ethanol proportion would ordinarily be expected to increase the blend's density, they said.

The OMCs argued that the discrepancies reinforced the need for independent testing using prescribed methods and appropriate reference samples.

The government and OMCs also challenged estimates that E20 fuel could cause annual consumer mileage losses of around Rs 62,000 crore and vehicle repair costs of Rs 39,000 crore, taking the combined estimated burden to approximately Rs 1.01 lakh crore.

Citing studies involving the Inter-Ministerial Committee, Indian Oil, the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), the ministry said the mileage impact varied depending on vehicle category and engine calibration.

Vehicles calibrated for E20 could experience mileage reductions of around 1-2 per cent, while certain other vehicles could see declines of 3-6 per cent, according to the Petroleum Ministry's response to concerns over ethanol blending published on August 12, 2025.

The OMCs said applying a blanket assumption of 10% mileage loss across the entire vehicle population was not scientifically established. They also sought supporting vehicle-performance data, materials compatibility studies and documented repair costs for the Rs 39,000 crore repair estimate.

More than 30 crore two-wheelers and 4 crore four-wheelers have been running on E20 fuel for over three years, while more than 6 crore people visit petrol pumps daily, the companies said, arguing that there had been no reported widespread incidence of vehicle breakdowns attributable to fuel quality.

India's ethanol-blending programme, which began with a pilot initiative in 2001, has become a key component of the country's strategy to reduce its dependence on imported crude oil, support agricultural incomes and improve energy security.

According to Petroleum Ministry figures, the programme since the 2014-15 ethanol supply year has generated foreign exchange savings of more than Rs 1.97 lakh crore, substituted approximately 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil and reduced carbon dioxide emissions by around 952 lakh metric tonnes.

It has also resulted in payments of more than Rs 1.66 lakh crore to farmers.

During the 2025-26 ethanol supply year, which ended on October 31, 2026, the three public sector OMCs procured 1,089 crore litres of ethanol and blended 1,134 crore litres against petrol sales of approximately 5,673 crore litres, the ministry said.

The companies rejected suggestions that they had a commercial incentive to blend ethanol beyond prescribed levels, saying additional procurement would increase their costs.

The controversy has implications for the credibility of India's ethanol-blending programme, which has been scaled up rapidly as part of efforts to cut oil imports and emissions. While the government cites energy security, environmental and agricultural benefits, questions over fuel quality and vehicle performance could influence consumer confidence and the pace of wider acceptance of E20.

The three OMCs have asked the Karnataka government to share complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the testing methodology. They have also sought access to counterpart samples for independent testing at an authorised laboratory using the prescribed referee method, in the presence of state government and OMC representatives.

The companies said they were willing to participate in a joint sampling and testing exercise and that any deviation established through the prescribed procedure would be dealt with under applicable guidelines. PTI ANZ

data.title: Employers, watchmen at California ports extend contract talks
data.description:
The Los Angeles and Long Beach seaports employer group and the International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26 extended their bargaining deadline through November 20, averting a potential strike by about 2% of workers at the busiest US container port complex.

  • The Pacific Maritime Association said on Friday that additional talks were scheduled with the union representing about 250 maritime watchmen at the ports.

  • Local 26 did not immediately return a request for comment.

  • The union watchmen control and inspect truck and employee entries at terminal gates, provide terminal security and guard and track critical cargo crossing the docks.

  • A strike by the ILWU watchmen would disrupt operations at terminals that handle roughly 85% of the cargo at Long Beach and 33% at Los Angeles, PMA said.

  • The Los Angeles and Long Beach ports each reported all-time cargo volume records for September. Those shipments included retail goods for holiday sales, equipment for AI data center construction and auto parts.

data.title: Ex-FBI counterintelligence agent stole almost $2.5M in crypto
data.description:
A former FBI counterintelligence agent admitted to wire fraud and money laundering in stealing almost $2.5 million in cryptocurrency from unidentified adversarial nations and wallets that were under investigation.

Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, used his investigative positions with access to FBI systems to steal cryptocurrency, then exchange and launder it through financial transactions to conceal its source and ownership.

Yaroch made about 100 fraudulent transfers related to 35 FBI investigations, gaining $2,474,380.66 in proceeds, according to a news release from the US Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of Virginia on Thursday.

He had earlier admitted to unauthorized transfers that involved about $1 million in digital assets, which was reported by Cointelegraph in August.

Yaroch paid off his debts and intended to use the proceeds to finance a new life in Portugal, where he planned to buy a vineyard, according to the statement.

The former agent admitted that his actions had compromised FBI investigations related to criminal groups and adversarial nations.

Yaroch faces up to 20 years in prison. His sentencing is set for March 4, 2027.

data.title: Fredun Pharmaceuticals Q2 results: Net profit jumps 90% on better demand
data.description:
Fredun Pharmaceuticals, a leading formulation manufacturer, reported that its net profit in the September quarter was up 90 per cent at ₹19 crore as compared to ₹10 crore in the same period last year on better demand.

Revenue was up 85 per cent at ₹266 crore (₹144 crore last year). EBITDA jumped 91 per cent to ₹43 crore (₹22 crore).

The company bought 26 per cent stake in Goodman Vetcare at a valuation of ₹300 crore in September. Goodman plans over 8 new stores and targets revenue of ₹100 crore by FY31.

In September 2026, Fredun acquired Furlicks from USV and its subsidiary Wellbeing Nutrition, marking its entry into pet wellness.

Furlicks makes easy-to-give oral strips covering skin and coat, gut health, joint care, calming, oral care and multivitamins.

The company plans to launch 16 new products over the next 6–9 months, taking the portfolio from 6 to 22 SKUs. The new launches will add formats such as cold-extruded, air-dried and freeze-dried products and functional biscuits.

Fredun launched a pet healthcare knowledge platform PAWTALKS with expert content on YouTube and Instagram.

Fredun Medhora, Managing Director, Fredun Pharmaceuticals, said the core formulations business was getting more efficient and added higher-margin while newer businesses in pet care, mobility, nutrition and dermaceuticals are now in a high-growth phase.

“These businesses carry better margins, so as they grow, they are steadily raising the quality of earnings. Fredun GX is now present in 19 states and pharmacies with distributors giving strong acceptance and repeat orders,” he said.

Pet care is one of the fastest-changing categories, as more pet parents treat their pets as family. The acquisition of stake in Goodman Vetcare and launch of PAWTALKS brings the company closer to a complete pet-wellness, he added.

“We are expanding capacity with the aim of building one of the largest manufacturing units at a single location in the country. We are also widening our product basket and strengthening the balance sheet,” he said.

data.title: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings files DRHP for IPO
data.description:
Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH), the parent company of Coca-Cola’s India bottling arm, Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages, has filed draft papers with SEBI to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 99.75 crore equity shares of face value ₹10 each by promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP). The equity shares are proposed to be listed on BSE and NSE.

India is among the top five markets for the Coca-Cola Company in terms of unit case volume. In June, the company had said it was exploring a potential listing of HCCH. This move is in line with the beverage major’s global asset-light strategy. This also comes after it divested 40 per cent stake in the company to Jubilant Bhartia Group, which became one of the promoters of HCCH in July 2025.

Currently, Coca-Cola through Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte. Ltd., holds 60 per cent of HCCH, while Jubilant Beverages Limited holds 40 per cent.

HCCH, which operates through its material subsidiary HCCB, is the largest bottler within the Coca-Cola System in India based on units of concentrate sold. For the three month period ended June 30, the company’s retained units recorded revenue from operations of ₹4,310.17 crore, registering a year-on-year growth of 20.46 per cent., while total sales volume grew by 18.61 per cent. Its portfolio includes various brands including Thums Up, Coca-Cola, Maaza, Kinley, Minute Maid and Sprite among others. As of June 30, the Company owned, controlled and operated a network of 14 production facilities, supplemented by 8 co-pack units.

Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Limited, Citigroup Global Markets India Private Limited, J.P. Morgan India Private Limited, Morgan Stanley India Company Private Limited, Axis Capital Limited, Goldman Sachs (India) Securities Private Limited and IIFL Capital Services Limited are the Book Running Lead Managers to the IPO. KFin Technologies Limited is the registrar to the offer.

data.title: AvenuesAI Q2 profit climbs 6% to ₹72 crore on higher demand
data.description:
AvenuesAI Ltd (formerly known as Infibeam Avenues), a multinational financial technology and AI infrastructure company headquartered in GIFT City, reported a six per cent rise in net profit in the September quarter to ₹72 crore while revenue increased 47 per cent year-on-year to ₹2,879 crore, on the back of growing demand.

The company’s operating performance was supported by growth in its payments business and expansion across digital financial services, even as competition in the payments market put pressure on transaction margins.

For the first half of FY27, revenue from operations increased 71 per cent to ₹5,560 crore, while profit after tax grew 24 per cent to ₹156 crore. Operating EBITDA, excluding other income, stood at ₹199 crore, registering a 19 per cent year-on-year growth.

CCAvenue, the company’s flagship payment gateway business, continued to drive transaction volumes. Its payment processing value increased 19 per cent sequentially to around ₹1.77 lakh crore during the September quarter. However, the net take rate moderated to 5.06 basis points, reflecting pricing pressure and heightened competition in the payments industry.

Expansion plans

Vishwas Patel, Managing Director and CEO, AvenuesAI, said the company was focusing on expanding its offerings beyond payment processing to deepen relationships with merchants and enterprises.

The company is also integrating Rediff.com into its digital ecosystem, with RediffOne targeting enterprise communication and digital services and RediffPay focusing on consumer payments.

International expansion of CCAvenue, particularly in the US, UAE, Saudi Arabia and Australia, is another growth priority.

AvenuesAI is also developing TISco, its AI-led transaction intelligence platform, to offer solutions in fraud detection, risk assessment and merchant intelligence.

The company is seeking to evolve from a payments-led business into a broader AI-first fintech platform, with technology-led services expected to support revenue diversification and improve margins over the longer term.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway's Quarterly Profit Falls After Investment Gains Shrink — WSJ
data.description:
By Krystal Hur

Berkshire Hathaway posted a 28% decline in quarterly net income after investment gains slumped and the conglomerate's insurance operations reported lower profits.

The Omaha, Neb.-based company continued to put more of its massive cash trove to work, repurchasing more of its own shares during the quarter.

Berkshire ended the third quarter with around $357 billion in cash and Treasury bills after accounting for a payable for purchasing some of the short-term government debt, a 2.1% decrease from three months earlier and the second-straight sequential drop.

The quarter also marked the end of Warren Buffett's long run as Berkshire's chairman. Buffett, 96, ceded the post to his son Howard Buffett in September. Greg Abel succeeded Buffett as CEO in January.

Net income fell to $22.11 billion, or $15,502 per Class A share, from $30.8 billion, or $21,413 a share, a year earlier.

The S&P 500 rose 2% during the third quarter, when U.S. Treasury yields surged.

Operating earnings, which exclude some investment results, slipped 5.8% to $12.71 billion from $13.49 billion. Profits from Berkshire's insurance-underwriting business fell sharply from a year ago, when the company benefited from a mild hurricane season and a turnaround from its auto insurer, Geico.

Berkshire's railroad and energy businesses reported higher profits, as did its portfolio of manufacturing, service and retailing companies.

Buffett has said that operating earnings are the better measure of the company's performance. Accounting rules require Berkshire to include unrealized gains and losses from its giant investment portfolio when it reports net income, meaning that short-term fluctuations in the stock market can cause big swings in quarterly income.

The company repurchased 4,536 Class A shares and 12,384,959 Class B shares during the third quarter, for around $9.6 billion.

Berkshire bought $2.4 billion of stocks during the September quarter and sold some $2.82.8 billion in the same period. Berkshire's largest holdings are Alphabet, American Express, Apple, Bank of America and Coca-Cola. The company is set to disclose more specifics on its stock portfolio in a regulatory filing later this month.

Berkshire's Class A shares are up more than 13% this year, and closed at a record high of around $869,301 on Wednesday.

The stock had previously been on a tumble after closing at a new high in May 2025, the day before Warren Buffett announced his retirement from the CEO post. But Berkshire rallied for much of October, as tech stocks began to slump amid fears over the AI build-out.

Write to Krystal Hur at krystal.hur@wsj.com

data.title: Berkshire ramps up buybacks in Q3 even as operating earnings dip
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) (BRK.B) has accelerated its stock buybacks during its third quarter ending Sept. 30, while the investing giant’s operating earnings fell amid weakness in its insurance businesses.

The Omaha, Nebraska-based conglomerate repurchased $9.6B in shares in Q3, ahead of Visible Alpha estimates of $1.6B, increasing its full-year stock buybacks to $14.4B.

Its Q3 buybacks have more than doubled from its Q2 2026 buybacks of $4.5B, which was also a sharp increase from its Q1 buybacks of $234M as the new CEO, Greg Abel, assumed leadership from billionaire investor Warren Buffett in January.

However, the company’s operating earnings for the period fell ~6% YoY to $12.7B, as operating earnings attributed to its insurance-underwriting business dropped ~43% YoY to $1.4B, driven by lower underwriting earnings at GEICO.

The vehicle and property insurance company added $982M in pre-tax underwriting earnings, down ~45% YoY, as its underwriting expenses rose ~17% YoY to $1.7B while losses and LAE jumped ~9% YoY to $8.7B.

The company's insurance-investment income, meanwhile, dropped ~14% YoY to $2.7B as interest and other investment income fell ~14% YoY mainly due to lower interest income, indicating lower short-term interest rates.

However, Berkshire's (BRK.A) railroad business, BNSF, added $1.7B with ~19% YoY growth, benefiting from higher shipping volumes and improved operating efficiencies, partially offset by higher fuel costs.

The company’s Energy business, meanwhile, generated $1.6B with an ~8% YoY growth thanks to higher earnings from the U.S. utilities and natural gas pipelines businesses. Its manufacturing, service, and retailing operations generated $4.0B with ~12% YoY growth driven by individual products and service businesses.

The company recorded $105.6B in revenue for the quarter, beating Visible Alpha estimates of $102B, with ~11% YoY growth as its insurance and other revenue climbed ~11% YoY to $91.0B.

data.title: Strive Reports $509M Quarterly Profit as Bitcoin Buying Accelerates
data.description:
TL;DR: Strive reported $509 million in third-quarter GAAP net income and said it purchased 8,136 BTC during the quarter, followed by another 15,124 BTC between October 1 and October 30. Its financing structure and accounting gains matter as much as the headline accumulation figures.

Bitcoin treasury company Strive has released a new set of numbers showing how rapidly its balance sheet has changed. In its November 6 third-quarter results, the Nasdaq-listed business reported $509 million in GAAP net income for the three months to September 30, alongside a large expansion of its Bitcoin position.

Strive said it acquired 8,136 BTC during the quarter and 20,373 BTC over the first nine months of 2026. It then bought another 15,124 BTC from October 1 through October 30. These are company-reported acquisition numbers, not an independent estimate of the market’s available Bitcoin supply.

Accumulation is only one side of the treasury story

The company reported $490.4 million in cash and cash equivalents as of October 30, plus a $50.1 million fair-value position in Strategy’s STRC preferred shares. It also closed an offering of seven million SATS preferred shares on October 20, reporting roughly $609 million in net proceeds after underwriting costs.

These details change how investors should interpret the Bitcoin buying. Purchasing more coins is easy to describe. The harder question is how those purchases are financed and how the resulting returns and risks are distributed among common and preferred shareholders. Preferred securities can provide capital, but they also introduce terms and obligations that differ from simply holding Bitcoin in a wallet.

That makes direct comparisons between treasury businesses difficult. NewsBTC recently reported Strategy’s purchase of another 811 BTC, a transaction accompanied by its own capital-management decisions. The underlying asset may be the same, but the capital structures are not.

Profit is not the same as operating cash generation

Strive’s GAAP profit is an accounting figure reflecting the company’s reported results under applicable rules. Bitcoin price changes can create substantial gains or losses in reported earnings without corresponding sales or cash receipts. Investors need to inspect the financial statements and reconciliations rather than assume a nine-figure profit represents operating cash generated from customers.

The company also disclosed a third-quarter Bitcoin yield of 18.5% and a year-to-date yield of 63.2%. Those are management-defined measures intended to assess Bitcoin growth relative to a particular share denominator. They are not conventional investment yields, cash dividends or guaranteed returns. As the share count and preferred capital change, the denominator matters enormously.

Strive said it was evaluating additional balance-sheet strategies spanning lending, brokerages, decentralised finance, reinsurance and tokenisation. Evaluating an opportunity is not the same as launching a product. Each area carries regulatory, counterparty or execution risks that could complicate an otherwise straightforward treasury narrative.

What shareholders should examine next

Three things deserve attention: updated fully diluted share counts, the costs and terms of preferred financing, and the company’s actual liquidity alongside its Bitcoin exposure. A rising coin balance is not sufficient evidence that every existing shareholder’s economic interest in those coins has increased.

The company’s November 6 release provides a useful dated snapshot rather than an assurance of future performance. NewsBTC’s reporting on the broader Bitcoin hashrate cycle is a reminder that the coin’s market and infrastructure operate beyond any one corporation’s strategy. For now, Strive has demonstrated aggressive accumulation. Whether it creates durable value for common shareholders will depend on capital discipline as much as on Bitcoin itself.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway accelerates stock buybacks, operating profit falls
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway accelerated stock repurchases in the third quarter, finding its own shares among the best assets to invest in its huge cash pile, while lower results from its insurance businesses weighed on overall profit.

The Omaha, Nebraska-based conglomerate said on Saturday it bought back $9.6 billion of stock in the quarter, on top of $4.8 billion earlier in the year, and about $2 billion more in the first four weeks of October.

Chief Executive Greg Abel has appeared more willing to spend Berkshire's cash than his predecessor Warren Buffett, who had difficulty finding things to buy toward the end of his 60 years at the helm. Berkshire ended September with $356.9 billion of cash and equivalents.

The July-September quarter was the third since Abel, 64, became chief executive. Buffett, 96, stepped down as chairman in September but remains chairman emeritus.

Quarterly operating profit fell 6% from a year earlier to $12.71 billion, or about $8,954 per Class A share.

Insurance was a major reason for the decline, as profit fell 26%. Underwriting profit fell 43%, and included a 45% pretax decline at the Geico insurer, where accident losses and advertising spending increased.

Net income fell 28% to $22.11 billion, including unrealized gains and losses on stocks that Berkshire still owns. Berkshire urges investors to ignore the volatility from changes in the values of stocks it is not selling.

SUPPORT FOR AI

Berkshire's cash holdings have declined from $380.2 billion at the end of March.

Its purchases this year have included billions of dollars of Alphabet shares to help Google's parent expand in artificial intelligence, though the stock trades below discounted prices that Berkshire paid.

Abel also spent $6.8 billion in July to buy home builder Taylor Morrison, and Berkshire has taken a 4% stake in Italian software technology company Bending Spoons .

Berkshire's biggest year for buybacks was 2021, when it repurchased $27 billion of stock.

data.title: The long, strange trip of Tesla's Cybertruck
data.description:
Elon Musk unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 with a stainless-steel, angular design that looked unlike any pickup on the road. The event at Tesla's design studio in Hawthorne, California invoked a Blade Runner theme.

Originally, Tesla promised a starting price under $40K, a 500-mile top range, and production by 2021. Delays, redesigns, and manufacturing problems pushed deliveries back until late November 2023, and prices came in far higher than promised. Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian was among the first owners.

An early public demo of the Cybertruck is remembered for the “armor glass” windows that shattered when a steel ball was thrown at them. The early Foundation Series cost around $100K, and Tesla later added a cheaper all-wheel-drive trim and a rear-wheel-drive version in 2025.

In reality, demand never matched the hype. While Tesla claimed more than a million reservations, those were refundable deposits, and actual sales were only a fraction of that ambitious tally. During an earnings conference call, Musk once stated Tesla could build 250K trucks a year, yet annual sales reportedly stayed far below that. Kelley Blue Book estimated Cybertruck sales of 39K in 2024 and just over 20K in 2025. The electric truck's reputation was also dented by repeated recalls, including problems with the accelerator pedal and body panels. Finally, analysts noted Elon Musk's high-profile political activity may have curbed some demand.

The Cybertruck entered a field of electric and conventional pickups. Its closest rivals were the Rivian R1T and the Ford F-150 Lightning. Chevrolet's Silverado EV and GMC's Hummer EV competed on range and luxury, and the Ram 1500 REV was another planned electric entrant. Of course, the Cybertruck also had to contend with the gas-powered F-150, Silverado, and Ram 1500, which have long dominated the truck market and offer more traditional towing and work capability.

Earlier in the week, Elon Musk said Tesla (TSLAA) will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production, which is Tesla's disruptive robotaxi. The future of the Cybertruck plans remains unclear, although Elon Musk confirmed it was the end of an era in a X reply. If the timeline holds, production would end roughly three and a half years after the first customer deliveries.

data.title: Berkshire Q3 Profit Down
data.description:
OMAHA (dpa-AFX) - Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. (BRK-A, BRK-B) reported on Saturday that its net earnings attributable to shareholders for the third quarter declined to $22.112 billion or $15,502 per class A share from $30.796 billion or $21,413 per class A share last year.

Investment gains for the third quarter dropped to $9.407 billion from $17.311 billion in the prior year.

Operating earnings for the quarter were $12.705 billion down from $13.485 billion in the previous year.

But total revenues for the quarter increased to $105.647 billion from $94.972 billion last year.

data.title: Bitcoin Developer Proposes a Quantum Trap for Hackers
data.description:
What if someone hacked your Bitcoin wallet and ended up paying you for the theft? That is the idea behind a proposal from Bitcoin Core developer Cory Fields.

As Bitcoin prepares for Q-Day, when powerful quantum computers could break its current cryptography, Fields wants to make stealing vulnerable coins a costly gamble.

On November 4, he introduced “quantum landmines” to the Bitcoin Development Mailing List. The idea is surprisingly simple: let Bitcoin owners secretly prepare traps that punish future hackers.

How Could a Bitcoin Hacker Lose Their Own Money?

Imagine you own 1 BTC in an old wallet vulnerable to quantum attacks.

Before Q-Day, you create a hidden proof of ownership inside a tiny quantum-safe Bitcoin output. Nobody else can see that proof.

  • Hackers must give Bitcoin to steal Bitcoin: Under the proposed rules, once quantum attacks become possible, anyone attempting to move that vulnerable 1 BTC must provide another 1 BTC as collateral. Both amounts then face a waiting period, potentially 30 days.
  • Hackers can steal, but you will get it back: If a quantum hacker steals your Bitcoin, you can reveal your secret proof during that window, recover your BTC and seize the hacker’s deposit.

The hacker loses money. You could walk away with twice your original holdings.

Fields argues that attackers would become “wary of stealing coins as they may be secretly guarded by mines.”

But There’s a Major Problem for Bitcoin Holders

The blockchain cannot distinguish a hacker from a legitimate owner. So everyone moving vulnerable Bitcoin would face the same collateral requirement.

Someone holding 10 BTC in an old wallet might need another 10 BTC in quantum-safe funds just to move their savings.

There is another complication – dormant Bitcoin, including Satoshi-era holdings.

If their private keys are lost, nobody can prepare a landmine. Fields proposes alternative auction mechanisms where bidders could challenge hackers and claim their deposits. One version would permanently destroy the vulnerable coins.

That raises difficult questions about ownership and Bitcoin’s supply.

For now, the debate exposes a difficult trade-off: protecting Bitcoin from future hackers could make moving older coins far more expensive for legitimate owners.

data.title: Tata Steel reports Rs 5,055 crore net profit in India business for Q2FY27
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Steel major Tata Steel recorded a profit after tax of Rs 5,055 crore from its Indian operations for the July-September quarter of the 2026-27 financial year (Q2FY27), supported by volume growth across domestic segments despite seasonal weakness and volatile global market conditions.

Consolidated revenues for the steelmaker stood at Rs 65,436 crore during the second quarter, while consolidated EBITDA reached Rs 10,665 crore, registering a 14 per cent quarter-on-quarter increase and a 17 per cent year-on-year growth. The overall consolidated net profit for the period stood at Rs 3,700 crore

On the domestic front, the company achieved revenues of Rs 42,653 crore and an EBITDA of Rs 10,634 crore, reflecting an operating margin of 25 per cent. Crude steel production in India expanded 7 per cent quarter-on-quarter to 6.18 million tons, while domestic deliveries climbed 16 per cent quarter-on-quarter to 5.98 million tons.

T V Narendran, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of Tata Steel, said, "We delivered strong growth in deliveries and earnings this quarter, backed by a resilient supply chain and close customer engagement, despite ongoing geoeconomic uncertainty and higher raw material costs. Deliveries grew 9% QoQ to ~7.92 million tons and EBITDA was up 14% QoQ to ~Rs 10,665 crores."

"India continued to be the cornerstone of our performance with volumes growing 16% QoQ despite a seasonally softer quarter, reflecting the strength of our market presence and customer reach. Our Automotive & Special Products vertical achieved 'best ever' 2Q volumes of ~1.1 million tons, driven by 26% growth in hi-end sales," he added.

Internationally, operations in the Netherlands posted revenues of 1,395 million euros and an EBITDA of 72 million euros, aided by the restart of the Direct Sheet Plant in August. The United Kingdom business recorded revenues of 411 million pounds, with an EBITDA loss of 56 million pounds amid subdued demand, elevated inventory levels, and higher imports.

Koushik Chatterjee, Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer, said, "Tata Steel delivered resilient performance in a volatile operating environment. Higher volumes in India and operational normalisation in the Netherlands helped offset elevated input costs. Consolidated EBITDA for the quarter rose 14% QoQ to Rs 10,665 crores and remained above Rs 13,000 per ton."

"This was primarily driven by strength of the India business, which delivered EBITDA of Rs 17,790 per ton and a margin of 25%, despite a seasonally softer quarter. Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited generated EBITDA of Rs 318 crores, and the amalgamation of NINL with Tata Steel remains on track for completion during the financial year, subject to final NCLT approval," Chatterjee stated.

For the half year, consolidated revenues stood at Rs 1,26,231 crore and EBITDA reached Rs 20,035 crore, representing a 21 per cent year-on-year rise. Tata Steel deployed Rs 3,280 crore toward capital expenditure during the quarter, bringing the half-year capex spend to Rs 6,860 crore, while net debt stood at Rs 91,423 crore with liquidity of Rs 40,076 crore.

data.title: Berkshire's Operating Earnings Fell 6%. Buybacks Hit $9.6B. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andrew Bary

Berkshire Hathaway's operating earnings fell 6% to $12.7 billion after taxes in the third quarter, depressed by weaker underwriting and investment income at the company's large insurance units.

Those declines were partly offset by higher profits at the conglomerate's railroad, utility and manufacturing and service businesses. The overall earnings figure is in line with the consensus estimate.

In its earnings release Saturday morning the company disclosed that it repurchased $9.6 billion of stock in the period, compared with $4.5 billion in the second quarter and probably its highest quarterly figure ever.

The buyback figure is above expectations and indicates that Berkshire CEO Greg Abel and controlling shareholder Warren Buffett felt the stock was inexpensive in the period.

There was a clue to the elevated buybacks in the third quarter, when the company repurchased about $3.4 billion of stock in July -a figure based on share-count figures from Berkshire's second-quarter 10-Q.

Berkshire shares have been on a roll for more than a month, rising 15% since the end of the third quarter and hitting new highs during the past week.

The class A shares ended Friday at $856,612 and the B shares at $570.89. Both classes are up about 13.5% so far this year.

This is a developing story. Please check back soon for more details and analysis.

Write to Andrew Bary at andrew.bary@barrons.com

data.title: India's oil ministry rejects Karnataka findings of excess ethanol in petrol
data.description:
India's petroleum ministry on Saturday rejected a report by authorities in the southern state of Karnataka that some petrol pumps there sold fuel with more ethanol than the 20% limit, saying its own tests showed supplies met national standards.

  • Four in five petrol pumps surveyed in India's southern state of Karnataka were selling fuel blended with ethanol content above the permitted 20% ​limit, a minister in the opposition-ruled state government said on Friday.

  • The findings had raised fresh ‌concerns about fuel quality as India expands the use of E20 fuel, a petrol blend consisting of 20% ethanol, as part of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's drive to reduce crude imports, lower emissions ​and support domestic ethanol producers.

  • Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi called the matter "petrol theft" and urged Modi to disclose actual ethanol levels and act against companies that over-blend.

  • The petroleum ministry questioned how the state government drew and tested its samples

  • It added that state-run fuel retailers Indian Oil Corporation , Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum had also disputed the findings and had sought independent testing of Karnataka's samples.

data.title: Meesho completes majority stake acquisition in Kirana Club and Retail Pulse Labs
data.description:
E-commerce platform Meesho Limited on Saturday, November 7, announced it has completed the first and second tranches of its acquisition of a 92.74% stake in Singapore-incorporated Kirana Club Pte. Ltd. and its Indian subsidiary, Retail Pulse Labs Private Limited (RPLPL), for an aggregate cash consideration of ₹186.71 crore.

Following the transaction, Kirana Club has become a direct subsidiary of Meesho, while RPLPL has become a step-down subsidiary of the listed company. The acquisition follows an initial agreement disclosed to stock exchanges on June 12, 2026, and was finalised for a total consideration of approximately ₹186.71 crore paid to identified selling shareholders.

In a regulatory filing, Meesho stated that the acquisition aligns with its strategic roadmap to strengthen its operational footprint and technological capabilities within the wider retail and e-commerce ecosystem. Both target entities operate in the B2B tech and community space for grocery retailers. Kirana Club focuses on proprietary software and digital community tools for grocers, while RPLPL runs a business-to-business marketplace connecting kirana and small merchants with FMCG brands and distributors across Tier 2 to Tier 4 towns and rural markets, generating income via commissions and advertising.

For the financial year ended March 31, 2026, RPLPL posted an annual turnover of ₹16.04 crore—up from ₹4.92 crore in the previous fiscal and ₹2.69 crore in the year prior—alongside a net loss of ₹1.60 crore. Singapore-based Kirana Club recorded a turnover of SGD 45,808 and a net loss of SGD 8.38 lakh during the same period, compared to SGD 38,177 in the preceding year.

Meesho promoters Vidit Aatrey and Sanjeev Kumar serve as directors on the boards of both Kirana Club and RPLPL, and both target entities will now be treated as related parties for future corporate dealings.

In the second quarter ended September 30, Meesho's consolidated net losses narrowed by 68% year-on-year to ₹132 crore from ₹411 crore, supported by advertising monetisation and logistics efficiencies.

During the July–September quarter, the platform's Net Merchandise Value (NMV) rose 23% year-on-year to ₹12,911 crore, while marketplace revenue from operations grew 34% to ₹4,120 crore. Meesho generated ₹345 crore in quarterly free cash flow, rebounding from an outflow of ₹226 crore in the preceding quarter on seasonal working capital benefits, bringing its cash balance to ₹7,048 crore as of September 30, 2026. Placed orders during the quarter expanded 17% year-on-year to 819 million, supported by an active base of 284 million annual transacting users and 1.13 million annual transacting sellers.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway accelerates stock buybacks, operating profit falls
data.description:
Berkshire Hathaway on Saturday reported a lower third-quarter operating profit as insurance underwriting results declined, and said it bought back $9.6 billion of stock in the quarter.

The repurchases are in addition to the $4.8 billion of stock that Berkshire repurchased earlier this year.

Quarterly operating profit fell 6% to $12.71 billion, or about $8,954 per Class A share, from $13.49 billion a year earlier.

Net income fell 28% to $22.11 billion, including unrealized gains and losses on stocks that Omaha, Nebraska-based Berkshire still owns.

data.title: Anthropic IPO to move forward despite tech selloff: FT
data.description:
Anthropic is pressing ahead with its plans for a U.S. public listing this month and is even prepared to accept a lower-than-expected valuation amid investor worries over an ongoing tech selloff, The Financial Times reported, citing multiple investors in the AI startup.

The Claude maker is racing towards its much-anticipated initial public offering before the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday this month, the investors said, adding that the company is planning to raise $80B-$100B at a valuation of $1.25T-$1.75T.

While that is a significant increase from its current $965B valuation, the target falls short of the doubled price tag investors had hoped for as recently as a month ago.

“My view is they will price it very conservatively, call it $1.5tn, and go up from there,” said one large investor. Others taking part in the deal expected even a lower valuation of roughly $1.3T.

Anthropic’s scaled-back expectations coincide with a sharp decline in AI-related tech stocks over the recent weeks, a selloff that accelerated on Thursday when the Nasdaq 100 plunged 6.4% on worries over a potential slowdown in AI infrastructure buildout.

Bloomberg reported on Friday that OpenAI , which recently delayed its IPO plans, completed a new private funding round of roughly $11B, valuing the ChatGPT maker at $1.25T, a sharp decline from $30B or more it initially sought at a $1.4T valuation.

However, according to more than half a dozen Anthropic investors, the company remains on track to go public even if its CEO Dario Amodei has to accept a price cut to achieve the goal.

“It’s just one milestone along the way,” one early investor of the company said. “They should treat it like every other fundraise: a means to an end.”

Multiple people familiar with Amodei’s thinking said that the CEO has shown little interest in beating Elon Musk’s SpaceX , which completed the largest ever IPO in June at a valuation of roughly $1.8T. “They don’t care about being bigger than SpaceX or maximizing the IPO,” one investor noted.

“They’re donating the majority of their economics to charity anyway,” he added, referring to Anthropic co-founders’ intention to hand 80% of their personal equity in the company to charitable purposes.

With $150B in cash and liquid investments on its balance sheet, Anthropic expects to raise enough funding so as not to sell equity again, people familiar with its thinking said.

“Public markets are highly averse to dilution,” added another large investor. “When you are taking a company public, that should be the last time you tap equity capital markets. But it opens the window for debt.”

JPMorgan , which leads U.S. retail sales of company shares, is expected to hold an “information session” for prospective investors on November 13, the FT said. Anthropic declined to comment on the report.

data.title: Ether ETFs Face Another $99.9M Outflow as Demand Stays Uneven
data.description:
TL;DR: US spot Ether ETFs posted a $99.9 million net outflow on November 5, Farside data show, following an $85.3 million outflow on November 3 and a temporary recovery on November 4. The pattern highlights a fragile demand picture, but cannot establish a direct forecast for ETH’s price.

Ether’s exchange-traded fund market is still searching for consistency. The latest fully reported daily figures in Farside Investors’ Ether ETF table show a $99.9 million net withdrawal on Thursday, November 5, just a day after the same group recorded a $53 million inflow. The reversal demonstrates why single-session data need context.

November 6’s table still contained unreported fields when reviewed, so it would be misleading to present the partial figure as a final market-wide total. A dated, complete session offers a better basis for an editorial assessment.

A brief rebound gave way to renewed redemptions

On November 5, BlackRock’s ETHA recorded a $75.2 million outflow and the firm’s ETHB line showed a further $22 million leaving. Fidelity’s FETH was down $2.2 million, while Grayscale’s ETHE showed a modest $500,000 withdrawal. Those figures add up to the $99.9 million negative session.

The previous day looked different. On November 4, the listed products collectively brought in $53 million, with positive flows in several funds offsetting negative readings elsewhere. Before that, November 2 and 3 brought losses of $139.7 million and $85.3 million respectively. The emerging picture is not a perfectly uninterrupted exodus. It is a market in which intermittent buying has yet to overcome repeated bouts of selling.

Our earlier report on November 2’s Ether ETF withdrawals provides a useful baseline. The subsequent sessions show that the pressure has persisted but has also varied substantially between days and issuers.

What ETF activity does and does not reveal

An ETF’s reported flow measures changes in the investment wrapper, not all Ethereum transactions. Institutions can obtain ETH exposure through spot holdings, derivatives, treasury companies and other vehicles. A negative day in the US listed fund category does not prove every sophisticated investor has turned bearish.

This is especially important for Ethereum because a significant share of the network’s economic activity occurs independently of an ETF. Stablecoin transfers, decentralised exchanges, tokenised assets and staking continue to operate whatever happens to a particular fund’s share count. The long-term investment case for ETH is often tied to that activity, but there is no automatic formula linking application usage to the token’s short-term price.

Concentration adds another layer. If one manager dominates the day’s net withdrawals, the aggregate should not be described as a consensus of all issuers. Analysts also need to separate price moves from flows: the dollar value of assets in a fund can fall because of market prices even when investors have not redeemed an equivalent amount of shares.

Two separate stories to follow

The first is whether ETF investors return in size and for more than a single session. The second is what happens in Ethereum’s development roadmap. The Ethereum Foundation announced a Glamsterdam testing delay on November 6, citing concerns about how proposed gas changes could affect existing applications. That is an engineering issue, not proof of a market-flow response, and it should be covered on its own terms.

For traders and longer-term holders, the practical takeaway is to compare several fully reported sessions, assess which issuers are driving the moves and resist treating flows as a stand-alone trading signal. Thursday’s number is meaningful evidence of weaker demand through US funds; it is not a reliable prediction of ETH’s next move.

This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
